correctness.summary: For F_nu(x)=x^(nu+1)e^(-x)I_nu(x), the logarithmic derivative and the Riccati equation for r=I_{nu+1}/I_nu give F''/F = 2-2r-2a/x+ar/x+a(a-1)/x^2 with a=2nu+1. At nu=-15/16 and x=2 this is 841/256-(39/16)r. Positive Bessel series and a geometric tail estimate give the exact lower bound r>58189629168/42817909615>841/624, hence F''(2)/F(2)<-23112816509/843183450880<0. This contradicts the second-derivative sign required by complete monotonicity. The rational certificate was recomputed with exact arithmetic.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Baricz (2010) explicitly asks whether x^(nu+1)e^(-x)I_nu(x) is SCM for all nu in (-1,-1/2]. Searches of the exact function and problem wording, synonymous complete-monotonicity formulations, the I_{nu+1}/I_nu ratio route, and citation chains did not locate a prior counterexample. Hornik--Grun (2013) studies sharp Amos-type ratio bounds but not this SCM question. Salazar (2026) revisits several Bessel-ratio open problems and a different Baricz complete-monotonicity transfer problem, but its stated resolved items do not include this Section 2(b) question. A differently phrased or non-indexed result remains possible.

value.summary: The result gives a rigorous negative answer to an explicit 2010 open problem using a simple rational order and an exact certificate rather than floating-point evidence. Continuity also shows that failure is robust on a nonempty open set of orders.

limitations: The full set of orders in (-1,-1/2] for which complete monotonicity fails is not classified.
The endpoints of the open failure neighborhood around -15/16 are not determined.
Parts (a) and (c) of the 2010 open problem are not addressed.
A differently phrased or non-indexed prior counterexample may exist.
Independent audit has not been performed.
